title: Satellite on‑prem checker journal
content:
Quick log + brain dump for Sat site runs — small checklist + gotchas I keep forgetting. Personal notes; copy trimmed for customer handover later.

SITE: Acme Biotech — satellite rack 2, room B3. Contact: Jordan Kline (on‑site).
OBJECTIVE: Finish 1st day smoke: network, storage mounts, system certs, API node join, runtime health.

TOPLINE STATUS (as of 2026-03-12 17:30 local):
- Basic infra up: switch & KVM, 2 x DGX-like nodes (A100 gen), edge LB.
- Blocker: MTU mismatch causing redis cluster flapping across hosts.
- Workaround in place: force mtu 9000 on all infra vlan interfaces until infra team patches spine.

PERSONAL CHECKLIST (tick as done):
- [x] Verify rack PDUs and sequence — avoid simultaneous power on for storage nodes.
- [x] Confirm NTP source (10.20.0.5) reachable and stratum OK.
- [x] BMC creds verified (local vault), BMC FW: 2.7.1 — note: older than recommended.
- [x] KMS endpoint validated (kms.acme.local) — thumbprint matches provided support doc.
- [ ] Reconcile split DNS entries for private.redwood.local -> missing PTR for api-02.
- [ ] Run full e2e generation test (10k tokens) and capture latency profile.

COMMANDS I RAN (keep these handy):
- quick MTU set (on each host):
  sudo ip link set dev eth1 mtu 9000
- flush iptables between test runs: sudo iptables -F && sudo nft flush ruleset
- join API node: ./redwood-join --env prod --token-file /etc/rw/token --region eu-north-1
- check kv cache: curl -s http://localhost:9411/debug/kvcache | jq .hits

NOTES / GOTCHAS (do not forget):
- Mellanox 2.40 drivers: reporting link resets if remote switch QoS enabled. If you see intermittent packet loss, check TOR switch firmware. Filed ticket with infra: INF-2219.
- SELinux default policy blocks /opt/redwood/runtime/tmp on some CentOS builds — temporary fix: setenforce 0 then relabel. Schedule proper policy patch before handover.
- HSM integration: customer uses AWS CloudHSM reachable over dedicated VPC peering. Need to confirm route propagation in Acme VRF — they use route-target filtering. If we rely on peering, ensure static route on their edge.
- Cert SANs: internal certs must include api.acme.internal and api.redwood.internal — they gave only first. Generated CSR locally and saved as csr-api-02.pem.

BLOCKERS / ACTIONS FOR NEXT RUN:
- Infra to confirm spine switch QoS patch (blocking redis flaps). Owner: Omar. ETA 2026-03-13 EOD.
- Platform patch: include mtu enforcement in node init script and fail gracefully with clear log. Create small PR. Owner: me (Marina).
- Ops: request PTR DNS change for api-02 (ticket created in DNS tracker).

MINOR IMPROVEMENTS / TODOS (notes to self):
- Add a tiny host check to the installer that verifies BMC FW >= 2.8 or warns.
- Add a guide snippet for KMS thumbprint retrieval to reduce back-and-forth with customer security.
- Add example nftables rules in our runbook; customers often use nft by default now.

FOLLOW UPS WITH CUSTOMER (short messages to send):
- "Jordan — saw MTU drift between TORs. Can you confirm if your infra team plans the QoS upgrade this week? If not, we'll pin 9000 on redwood nodes to keep cluster stable."
- "Also noticed HSM route is missing in VRF; sharing recommended static route to add (will paste route block)."

RANDOM OBSERVATIONS (for later writeup):
- On this hardware, kernel 5.15 + mlx 5.4 combination seemed more stable in short tests vs 5.10. Worth noting in onboarding doc.
- Latency outliers during batch tests correlate with backup windows on NAS (they run at 02:00 local). Ask them for a quieter window for heavy perf tests.

SNIPPET: post‑run sanity command I keep typing:
- curl -sS http://api-01.internal:8080/healthz | jq -r '.status, .uptime'

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (put on ticket or slack):
- Does Acme want us to manage certificate rotation or hand them a cron that calls cert-manager? (ask CS)
- Should we default to mtu 9000 in the installer for all onprem, or make it opt-in? Pros: fewer issues; Cons: possible incompat with older gear.

END NOTES: Keep this as a running personal journal during the field sprint. When cleaned up, extract: 1) customer handover checklist, 2) infra playbook addendum, 3) installer followups (PRs).

Last quick log entry: packed a small USB with: csr-api-02.pem, cert-ca-acme.pem, kms-thumbprint.txt, installer-args.txt (copy in /tmp/sat-pack).

-- M.C."
